chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al-Halby, who said:

I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about a man who circumambulated the House, then [performed sa'i] between As-Safa and Al-Marwa, and he had performed Tamattu', then he hastened and kissed his wife before he shortened [his hair] from his head. So he (peace be upon him) said: 'Upon him is blood to spill; and if he copulated, then upon him is a camel or a cow.'

key_terms.تَمَتَّعَ: Performed Tamattu' (a type of Hajj where one performs Umrah first, then Hajj)
key_terms.دَمٌ: Blood (referring to a sacrificial animal, typically a sheep)
key_terms.يُهَرِيقُهُ: To spill (the blood of the sacrifice)

ai.seo_question: What is the penalty for a pilgrim in Hajj al-Tamattu' who has intercourse before shaving his head?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that the penalty for premature intimacy during Hajj al-Tamattu' is determined by the degree of sexual act: mere contact incurs the blood of a sheep (dam), while full intercourse demands a heavier sacrifice of a camel or cow. This ruling underscores the principle that the state of Ihram remains binding until the ritual haircut (qasr) is performed, distinguishing between minor and major breaches of the pilgrimage's sanctity.
